stem: A healthcare study measures average patient recovery rate across 3 hospitals, each containing multiple departments. hospital A has 5 observations with mean 50.6 % (within-hospital SD = 4.8). hospital B has 8 observations with mean 32.8 % (within-hospital SD = 4.7). hospital C has 20 observations with mean 40.1 % (within-hospital SD = 5.7). The between-hospital standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 6.0 and 15.0 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true average patient recovery rate for hospital A, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-hospital variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for hospital A: 50.1 % (shrunk from raw 50.6). Range [49.4, 50.4] as between-hospital SD varies from 6.0 to 15.0. Pooled mean: 39.9.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 39.9 % (weighted average of 3 hospital means).
Shrinkage factor for hospital A: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=10.0: B = 0.956.
Interval [49.4, 50.4] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (50.6) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (39.9) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
